actions_performed: Inspected the RHEL release, kernel, installed GNU tar, archive contents, restore request, live-file metadata, and checksums.
Validated both requested paths as safe, unique, missing from live/, and present exactly once in the archive.
Selectively extracted only invoices/INV-100.txt and invoices/INV-101.txt while preserving their file modes.
Verified the exact live-file set, protected customer-register checksum, invoice bytes and modes, and source-archive checksum.
Restarted node1 safely and verified its changed boot identity, system health, services, kernel, and restored data.

evidence.requirement: Restore the requested invoice bytes and modes without unrelated archived files
evidence.summary: Both requested invoices match their archive members byte-for-byte, have mode 0644, and the exact live regular-file set contains only customers.csv and those two invoices; old-notes.txt is absent.

evidence.requirement: Retain the current newer customer register
evidence.summary: The customer register retained its original SHA-256 checksum 0f060a93ce03b8a38e00181862fc775d127160011235f60f4d040afd98e84d51 before restoration, after restoration, and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: Used the already-installed GNU tar 1.35 on RHEL 10.0. The kernel remained 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 after restart; no packages or OS components were changed.

Healthy baseline boot ID was 6ab6a71b-188c-48ae-971b-a6bb378b1d72; safe restart was acknowledged; post-restart boot ID changed to 2f97cabf-70b3-4a66-9a5a-6e9bdb5f7e18. The system returned to running state with sshd and chronyd active, no failed units, and all required data, modes, checksums, and exact file-set checks passing.
